To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Brazil has developed an ambitious set of science, technology and innovation policy measures aimed at the pharmaceutical industry, labelled the ‘Health-Industry Complex’ (CIS); (2) the CIS was an outcome of incremental change, backed by the sustained and coordinated efforts of a group of public health professionals; (3) as experts with a particular view of health, innovation and industrial policy came to dominate key health institutions, they shaped government responses to new challenges.

the Brazilian government's efforts to promote innovation in the pharmaceutical industry are a result of a series of incremental policy changes, backed by the sustained work of public health professionals.
the CIS was an outcome of incremental change and that public health professionals were the main agents of change in the Brazilian government.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the Brazilian state has been able to integrate science and technology policies into the health sector and how it has done so in the context of a rapidly changing global pharmaceutical industry.

the ways in which public health experts have shaped Brazil's science, technology and industrial policies in the last two decades, and how they did so without the support of an executive that is usually seen as a major force in the formulation of Brazilian health policy.
the conditions that enable public health professionals to become policy agents and to shape the agenda of a large, complex bureaucracy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CIS is a result of the efforts of public health experts who have managed to shape the Brazilian government's health policies, in spite of the country's political instability.
the CIS is a result of incremental change in the Brazilian health policy and it has been backed by a group of public health professionals.
Brazil is a country with an ambitious and innovative health policy, which is being developed through the incremental and sustained efforts of a group of public health professionals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
incremental change, rather than partisan orientation, was the key factor in the evolution of Brazil's health-industry complex.
incremental changes in policy, rather than a partisan shift in government, are a key feature in the Brazilian case.
the CIS is an incremental policy change, and that the role of public health professionals in this process is key to understanding it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
incremental policy change can be an outcome of the sustained efforts of policy entrepreneurs, even in a highly centralised political system.
public health professionals have played a key role in the incremental development of the CIS and that this role is unlikely to be reversed in the short term.

the CIS was the result of a sustained effort by public health experts to promote a specific vision of science and technology policy within the Ministry of Health and the executive, which was then institutionalised through the creation of new institutions and the reform of others.
